content: Khalid Abdulkerim is a Full Stack Web Developer and a third-year Computer Science and Engineering student from Worabe in the Central Ethiopia Region of Ethiopia. He recently completed the Full Stack Web Development program at Evangadi Tech, where he gained hands-on experience building modern web applications using React, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and AI technologies.

Khalid discovered his passion for software development after following Ethiopian software engineers such as Ezedin Kamil and Mukerem Ali. His interest grew significantly after joining the Computer Science and Engineering Club (CSEC Lab) at Adama Science and Technology University, where he was surrounded by students actively building technology projects.

Khalid initially started programming through competitive programming. Over time, he became more interested in solving real-world problems and realized that web applications provide one of the fastest ways to build products that people can immediately use. This motivated him to pursue full stack web development.

Khalid enjoys transforming ideas into real software products. His motivation comes from curiosity, solving meaningful problems, building useful applications, continuous learning, and creating technology that positively impacts society.

Khalid's long-term goal is to become a software engineer who builds impactful technology rather than simply writing code for income. He hopes to solve important community problems through software while continuously improving his technical and engineering skills.

Khalid is currently focused on improving his full stack development skills, building production-ready applications, exploring AI-powered software, and preparing for freelance opportunities and professional software engineering roles.

Khalid primarily works with JavaScript, React, Node.js, Express.js, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. He is comfortable designing REST APIs, building responsive frontend applications, integrating authentication systems, and developing complete full-stack applications.

On the frontend, Khalid builds responsive user interfaces using React, modern JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, and component-based architecture. He focuses on usability, responsiveness, accessibility, and clean UI implementation.

On the backend, Khalid develops RESTful APIs using Node.js and Express.js. He has experience implementing authentication, authorization, database integration, file uploads, AI service integration, and server-side application architecture.
Khalid has experience designing relational database schemas, creating efficient SQL queries, defining relationships, and working with PostgreSQL and MySQL for production-style applications.

Khalid has practical experience integrating Generative AI into applications using Google's Gemini API. His work includes Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), semantic search, document chunking, vector embeddings, prompt engineering, and AI-assisted user experiences.

When implementing a new feature, Khalid first understands the requirements, breaks the work into manageable tasks, plans the backend architecture and data flow when necessary, implements the backend and frontend incrementally, and thoroughly tests the completed feature before considering it finished.

Khalid approaches debugging methodically by carefully reading error messages, reproducing the issue, inspecting browser DevTools and backend logs, using console logging when appropriate, testing APIs with Postman, consulting official documentation, and only then using AI tools to validate ideas or explore alternative solutions.

Khalid learns new technologies by first understanding the fundamentals through official documentation and trusted resources, then reinforcing that knowledge by building practical projects. He believes hands-on experience is the best way to master new tools and frameworks.

Khalid values writing clean, maintainable, and understandable code. He prefers understanding how a solution works instead of copying code blindly and aims to produce software that is easy to extend and maintain.

Khalid uses AI tools such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini as development assistants. He relies on them for learning concepts, debugging, brainstorming, refactoring, documentation, and reviewing ideas while ensuring he fully understands every solution before incorporating it into his projects.

The AI Powered Evangadi Forum is Khalid's flagship full-stack project. Inspired by Stack Overflow, it allows users to ask questions, answer discussions, authenticate securely, search intelligently, receive notifications, and interact with an AI assistant.

Key features include question posting, answering, voting-ready architecture, semantic search, Google OAuth, JWT authentication, role-based authorization, notifications, AI-powered document question answering, responsive design, and an administrative document management system.

The forum contains a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system. Uploaded documents are automatically processed into chunks, converted into vector embeddings, stored in the database, retrieved using semantic similarity, and provided to Google's Gemini model to generate grounded answers.

The forum supports semantic search using vector embeddings, allowing users to find related questions based on meaning rather than exact keywords. This improves discoverability and reduces duplicate questions.

Khalid extended the original bootcamp project by implementing AI-powered features including the RAG pipeline, semantic search, Google authentication, notifications, responsive UI improvements, and several backend enhancements.

Khalid's portfolio website is itself a technical project. Besides showcasing his work, it includes an AI-powered chatbot built with Retrieval-Augmented Generation, markdown rendering, typing animation, SEO optimization, responsive design, and project-specific knowledge retrieval.

The Apple website clone was built to strengthen responsive web design skills, component-based UI development, layout techniques, and attention to visual detail while recreating a professional commercial website.

The PERN Todo application helped Khalid strengthen his understanding of CRUD operations, RESTful API development, PostgreSQL database management, frontend-backend communication, and full-stack application architecture.

While implementing Google OAuth, Khalid encountered configuration issues involving redirect URIs, client credentials, and authentication flow. Solving these problems deepened his understanding of OAuth and strengthened his debugging skills.

Building the RAG system taught Khalid that retrieval quality depends heavily on document chunking, embedding generation, prompt design, and semantic retrieval. Improving these components significantly increased the relevance of AI-generated responses.

Khalid enjoys solving difficult engineering problems by breaking them into smaller pieces, experimenting with possible solutions, reading documentation, and iterating until he understands both the problem and the final implementation.
Khalid is currently open to software engineering opportunities, freelance projects, and collaborative work involving full-stack web development and AI-powered applications.
The best way to contact Khalid is through the contact form on this portfolio website or by email at kalidabdu921@gmail.com.

Khalid plans to continue deepening his expertise in backend engineering, distributed systems, artificial intelligence, cloud technologies, and scalable software architecture while building products that solve real-world problems.
